articles.title: Senate What If
articles.summary: There is a fierce battle unfolding over control of the Senate, with the chamber up for grabs in November. Map out each party’s path to the Senate majority with NBC News’ “Senate What If” tool.
articles.body:
There is a fierce battle unfolding over control of the Senate, with the chamber up for grabs in November.

Republicans currently have a 53-47 majority, and Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of the chamber — meaning they have to keep all the seats they currently hold and flip four more. Though the battleground is more favorable to Republicans, the GOP is on defense this year. Of the 35 Senate seats up for election, Republicans control 22 and Democrats control 13.

You can map out each party’s path to the Senate majority with NBC News’ “Senate What If” tool below. Or explore different scenarios from NBC News’ chief data analyst Steve Kornacki and “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker.

In this scenario, Republicans lose seats in the midterms as voters look for a check on an unpopular president. Texas elects a Democratic senator for the first time since 1988. Former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown reclaims a Senate seat in Ohio, and North Carolina flips for the Democrats, too. But control of the Senate hangs in the balance as we wait for Alaska mail ballots to come in from around the rural state and be tabulated — a process that can take days.

If incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan triumphs, Republicans keep control of the Senate, with Vice President JD Vance as the tiebreaking vote. A victory for former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola, on the other hand, would tip the balance for Democrats.

Steve Kornacki: Michigan thwarts Democratic hopes

Broad Democratic gains across the map in North Carolina, Ohio, Texas and Alaska provide a strong midterm mandate for the party. But the progressive campaign of Democrat Abdul El-Sayed falls short in battleground Michigan, and voters elect Republican Mike Rogers as their next senator, thwarting a chance for Democrats to control the Senate.

Republicans keep their majority, albeit narrowly, with Vice President JD Vance serving as the tiebreaking vote.

Kristen Welker: Democrats notch a narrow win

A narrow Democratic majority would involve Democrats holding their current battlegrounds in Georgia and Michigan, and flipping four GOP-held seats while falling short in some deeply Republican states. In this scenario, Democrats flip Maine, the one Senate seat held by a Republican in a state Trump lost in 2024, and North Carolina, the closely divided battleground state.

Under this scenario, Democrats would pick up two more seats in Republican-leaning states where the individual candidates have defined the contours of the race — Ohio, where former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown is looking to make a comeback, and Texas, where Republican Ken Paxton is trying to unite Republicans who did not support him in the primary.

Republicans could hang on to the narrowest of majorities even if Democrats flip a few seats. Say Democrats are able to flip North Carolina, Maine and Ohio, and each party holds on to its other battleground states. That would result in a 50-50 Senate, giving Republicans control since Vice President JD Vance casts tiebreaking votes in the chamber.

In a tied Senate, both parties would enter a power-sharing agreement, evenly dividing committee membership, and a single senator could have enormous sway. If this happens, keep an eye on Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, who recently suggested he could rethink his status as a Democrat, saying at the Texas Tribune Festival, “Let’s revisit after the midterm and see what happens if I happen to be 51.”

Kristen Welker: Republicans grow their majority

Democrats may have the momentum, but this scenario is an important reminder of how the path to the Senate runs through some very Republican territory. In this case, Republicans hang on in red states like Iowa, Ohio and Texas, while GOP incumbent Sen. Susan Collins once again overcomes political headwinds. And while Democrats win in North Carolina, Republicans capitalize on the open seats in Michigan and New Hampshire.

A blockbuster night for Democrats would involve flipping multiple seats in deeply Republican states and holding on to their battleground seats in Michigan and Georgia. In a favorable environment, Democrats would flip Maine, the only Republican-held seat in a state that Trump lost in 2024, and North Carolina, a closely divided state.

Democrats would also pick up Alaska and Texas. And several Republicans would lose in the heartland, where farmers have struggled with tariffs and high diesel prices, including Ohio, Iowa, Kansas and Nebraska. But a Republican loss in Nebraska wouldn’t necessarily be a Democratic win — independent Dan Osborn has said he would not caucus with either party.

articles.title: O que abre e fecha em Maceió no feriado de Finados e Servidor | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidades de saúde, Centrais JÁ! e trens terão mudanças no funcionamento durante o feriadão; shoppings e comércio do Centro terão horários especiais.
articles.summary: O que abre e fecha em Maceió no feriadão de Finados e do Servidor Público envolve mudanças nos horários de shoppings, trens, comércio e unidades de saúde da capital.
articles.body:
Cemitério São José Dia de Finados Maceió — Foto: Nick Marone

O feriadão do Dia do Servidor Público, celebrado na sexta-feira (30), e do Dia de Finados, na segunda-feira (2), vai alterar o funcionamento de serviços públicos, comércio e transporte em Maceió .

Os serviços afetados retomam o atendimento normal na terça-feira (3). Confira abaixo o que abre e o que fecha na capital alagoana durante o feriado prolongado.

As Unidades de Saúde e os Centros de Atenção Psicossocial (Caps) estarão fechados na sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2). Os atendimentos serão retomados na terça-feira (3).

Os pontos fixos de vacinação do Maceió Shopping e do Pátio Shopping não funcionarão na sexta-feira (30). No sábado (31), o atendimento será das 12h às 20h.

Os locais voltarão a fechar no domingo (1º) e na segunda-feira (2), com retomada dos serviços na terça-feira (3).

As unidades do Saúde da Gente Especialidades, no Benedito Bentes e no Salgadinho, estarão fechadas na sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2). Os atendimentos serão retomados na terça-feira (3).

Na unidade do Salgadinho, os agendamentos previstos para o dia 30 de outubro foram transferidos para 13 de novembro.

O CCZ não terá atendimento administrativo na sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2), mas manterá um plantão das 8h às 16h para denúncias e possíveis apreensões de animais.

O contato pode ser feito pelo WhatsApp (82) 3312-5492. O atendimento administrativo será retomado na terça-feira (3).

Os demais serviços administrativos da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde também estarão suspensos nos dois dias.

Todas as Centrais JÁ! estarão fechadas na sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2). O atendimento será retomado na terça-feira (3).

As agências dos Correios funcionarão normalmente na sexta-feira (30) e estarão fechadas na segunda-feira (2), Dia de Finados.

As unidades que abrem aos sábados manterão o funcionamento habitual. O atendimento será retomado na terça-feira (3).

Centro de Atendimento ao Turista (CAT Mercado)

O Centro de Atendimento ao Turista, localizado no Mercado da Produção, não funcionará na sexta-feira (30) nem na segunda-feira (2). O atendimento será retomado na terça-feira (3), das 8h às 14h.

Não haverá circulação comercial de trens em Maceió na segunda-feira (2), Dia de Finados. As operações serão retomadas normalmente na terça-feira (3).

As lojas âncoras, lojas satélites, quiosques e praças de alimentação funcionarão das 9h às 22h. Os estabelecimentos da Varanda Gourmet abrirão das 11h30 às 22h.

Lojas, quiosques, praça de alimentação e supermercado funcionarão das 9h às 22h. A academia Smart Fit abrirá das 7h às 19h.

Lojas, quiosques, praça de alimentação, restaurantes e espaços de lazer funcionarão das 10h às 22h.

Segundo a Sociedade Aliança Comercial de Maceió, as lojas do Centro funcionarão das 9h às 14h na segunda-feira (2).

articles.title: Estudo aponta que Centro de São Luís registra mais horas de calor intenso que a Avenida Litorânea | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa desenvolvida por pesquisadores da Uema e da UFMA identificou diferença de 4h30 no período de muito calor entre as duas áreas e apontou influência da velocidade dos ventos na sensação térmica.
articles.summary: Iniciativa desenvolvida por pesquisadores da Uema e da UFMA identificou diferença de 4h30 no período de muito calor entre as duas áreas.
articles.body:
Avenida Litorânea em São Luís — Foto: A.Baeta

Os impactos das mudanças climáticas no planeta reforçam a importância de estudar como o calor afeta a população nas cidades. Em São Luís, uma pesquisa da Universidade Estadual do Maranhão (Uema) identificou condições de desconforto térmico mais intensas no Centro da capital do que na Avenida Litorânea , onde a circulação dos ventos ajuda a amenizar o calor.

No Centro, o período classificado como de “muito calor” dura, em média, quatro horas e 30 minutos a mais por dia do que na Avenida Litorânea. Os dados são de um estudo publicado na Revista Brasileira de Geografia, periódico do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

A pesquisa foi desenvolvida pela professora Maria Iranilde Almeida Costa Pinheiro, da Uema, em coautoria com Juarez Mota Pinheiro, da Universidade Federal do Maranhão (UFMA).

O trabalho analisou como fatores meteorológicos, principalmente a velocidade dos ventos, influenciam a sensação térmica em diferentes áreas da capital maranhense.

Para comparar os dois locais, os pesquisadores instalaram equipamentos de monitoramento nas proximidades da Biblioteca Pública Benedito Leite, no Centro, e do Círculo Militar, na Avenida Litorânea. As medições foram realizadas em cinco campanhas, com registros de variáveis meteorológicas durante períodos de 24 horas.

A análise utilizou o índice Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET), empregado para avaliar o conforto térmico humano em ambientes externos.

Com base nos dados coletados, os pesquisadores classificaram as condições observadas em quatro categorias: conforto , pouco calor , calor e muito calor .

Centro registra maior desconforto térmico

Estudo aponta que Centro de São Luís registra mais horas de calor intenso que a Avenida Litorânea — Foto: Divulgação/UEMA/UFMA

O índice PET apresentou média de 30,7°C no Centro e de 26°C na Avenida Litorânea, uma diferença de 4,7°C. O indicador considera variáveis meteorológicas e a resposta fisiológica humana para estimar a sensação térmica em ambientes externos.

O estudo também identificou diferenças na velocidade média dos ventos entre os dois locais. No Centro, o vento atingiu aproximadamente 0,5 metro por segundo. Na Avenida Litorânea, a média foi de 3,5 metros por segundo.

Segundo os pesquisadores, a diferença na circulação dos ventos ajuda a explicar as condições térmicas mais desfavoráveis registradas na região central.

Estudo pode contribuir para o planejamento urbano

A pesquisa destaca a importância de considerar as características da ocupação urbana e a circulação dos ventos no planejamento dos espaços públicos. Em cidades de clima tropical quente e úmido, esses fatores podem influenciar as condições térmicas percebidas pela população.

Entre as estratégias que podem contribuir para melhorar o conforto térmico estão a ampliação de áreas verdes, a arborização, a preservação de espaços naturais e o planejamento adequado das áreas públicas.

O conforto térmico também está relacionado à qualidade de vida, à saúde pública e à adaptação das cidades às mudanças climáticas. Além disso, pode influenciar o uso dos espaços urbanos para atividades econômicas e turísticas.

articles.title: Trio de colombianos é preso suspeito de furtar farmácias em Jundiaí | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Guarda Municipal, duas mulheres e um homem saíram da capital para furtar comércios na região de Jundiaí. GM informou que os suspeitos têm passagens pelo crime em outros locais do país.
articles.summary: Furto em farmácias em Jundiaí (SP) termina com a prisão de três colombianos que usavam bolsas com papel-alumínio para furtar R$ 6 mil em cosméticos e suplementos.
articles.body:
Três colombianos, sendo um homem e duas mulheres, foram presos em flagrante pela Guarda Municipal (GM) de Jundiaí (SP) na quarta-feira (28) suspeitos de furtar farmácias na cidade. Câmeras de monitoramento registraram a ação do grupo.

Segundo a Guarda, as equipes foram alertadas pela central de rádio sobre uma série de furtos que vinham ocorrendo em drogarias do município. Com base nas características informadas, os guardas iniciaram buscas e localizaram os suspeitos no momento em que eles saíam de uma farmácia na Rua do Retiro.

O trio pretendia fugir em um carro vermelho estacionado nas proximidades. De acordo com a Guarda Municipal, o veículo não estava registrado no nome de nenhum dos envolvidos.

Durante a revista, os agentes apreenderam cosméticos e medicamentos, incluindo protetores solares e suplementos voltados a gestantes. O prejuízo total dos itens levados foi estimado entre R$ 5 mil e R$ 6 mil. Nenhuma arma foi encontrada com o grupo.

De acordo com o guarda Renan, que participou da ocorrência, os suspeitos confessaram que viajaram da capital até o interior de SP para cometer os crimes.

"Eles declararam que vieram de São Paulo para praticar os furtos na região de Jundiaí. Eles dizem que por aqui na região seria mais fácil praticar os furtos. Por ser interior, acharam que seria mais tranquilo para praticar esses atos", comentou o GCM.

As investigações e as imagens do circuito interno de segurança apontam que os suspeitos agiram em ao menos duas farmácias: uma localizada no bairro Engordadouro e outra na Rua do Retiro.

Trio é preso em flagrante suspeito de furtar farmácias em Jundiaí — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Para tentar escapar do flagrante na saída das lojas, o trio utilizava um artifício na bolsa. "Encontramos com eles uma bolsa que estava com o forramento de alumínio, que eles geralmente usam para burlar o sistema de alarme", destacou o guarda.

Ainda conforme a Guarda Municipal, um dos envolvidos já possuía Cadastro de Pessoa Física (CPF) emitido no Brasil. Após a checagem detalhada dos dados no sistema, foi constatado que os três têm passagens policiais anteriores pelo crime de furto no país.

O homem e as duas mulheres foram levados ao Plantão Policial, onde foram presos em flagrante por furto qualificado.

articles.title: Carne Wagyu: o que torna esse corte tão especial e como preparar em casa | G1
articles.standfirst: De origem japonesa, a carne conquista pelo marmoreio, pela maciez e pelo sabor marcante; veja como escolher os cortes, acertar o preparo e harmonizar com acompanhamentos e bebidas.
articles.summary: De origem japonesa, a carne conquista pelo marmoreio, pela maciez e pelo sabor marcante; veja como escolher os cortes, acertar o preparo e harmonizar com acompanhamentos e bebidas.
articles.body:
Você coloca na boca e ela derrete. Seu sabor é inigualável e sua maciez não possui igual. A carne de Wagyu é atualmente uma das maiores experiências gastronômicas do mundo e sucesso nos principais restaurantes, além de ser objeto de desejo de quem gosta da boa comida.

De origem japonesa, a carne do tipo Wagyu não demorou para conquistar o Brasil, um país apaixonado por churrasco e que sabe absorver o que é bom da gastronomia mundial.

Para quem deseja experimentar essa carne, a escolha do fornecedor é um dos primeiros cuidados. No Ítalo Supermercados, é possível encontrar Wagyu da Guidara, marca brasileira especializada em carnes nobres. A empresa trabalha com seleção genética e criação de animais da linhagem Wagyu no Brasil, oferecendo produtos com diferentes características de marmoreio, maciez e sabor.

A procedência merece atenção porque nem toda carne anunciada como Wagyu tem a mesma origem ou composição genética. Existem exemplares puros, animais cruzados com a linhagem e produtos importados do Japão, categorias que apresentam diferenças e precisam estar corretamente identificadas. Comprar de fornecedores confiáveis, que informem a marca, o corte e a categoria da carne, ajuda a evitar ofertas enganosas e permite escolher o produto de acordo com a experiência desejada.

Mas o que faz essa carne ser tão diferente das demais? A resposta está em uma combinação de genética, criação cuidadosa e uma característica que chama a atenção logo no primeiro olhar: o marmoreio, nome dado aos pequenos veios de gordura distribuídos entre as fibras musculares. É essa gordura intramuscular que contribui para a suculência, a textura macia e o sabor rico que tornaram o Wagyu conhecido internacionalmente.

A história do Wagyu, da tradição japonesa à gastronomia mundial

A palavra Wagyu significa, literalmente, “gado japonês”. A história da carne está ligada à criação de bovinos no Japão, onde os animais foram utilizados durante séculos principalmente como força de trabalho na agricultura.

Com as transformações da sociedade japonesa e o crescimento do consumo de carne bovina no Japão, a criação passou por processos de seleção e aprimoramento genético que ajudaram a consolidar as características das raças conhecidas atualmente como Wagyu.

O Japão reconhece quatro raças principais: Japanese Black, Japanese Brown, Japanese Shorthorn e Japanese Polled. Entre elas, a Japanese Black é responsável pela maior parte da produção japonesa e se destaca pelo marmoreio intenso.

A partir das últimas décadas do século 20, animais da linhagem Wagyu começaram a ser criados também em outros países, incluindo Austrália, Estados Unidos e Brasil. Com isso, a carne ganhou espaço em restaurantes especializados, churrascarias e cozinhas que valorizam ingredientes premium.

Por que a carne Wagyu é tão macia e saborosa?

A principal característica do Wagyu é o marmoreio. Ao contrário da gordura concentrada apenas na parte externa da peça, ela aparece entre as fibras musculares, formando desenhos que lembram os veios de uma pedra de mármore.

Durante o preparo, parte dessa gordura derrete e contribui para a sensação de suculência. O resultado é uma textura delicada, um sabor pronunciado e uma experiência diferente daquela proporcionada por cortes bovinos mais magros.

O marmoreio também influencia a percepção do sabor. A gordura transporta compostos aromáticos e, quando combinada à carne, ajuda a produzir notas que podem lembrar manteiga e nozes, dependendo do animal, da alimentação, do corte e do grau de marmoreio.

Isso não significa que quanto mais gordura, melhor será a experiência para qualquer pessoa. O Wagyu mais marmorizado tem sabor mais intenso e textura quase amanteigada, mas pode ser pesado para quem prefere carnes magras. A escolha do corte e do nível de marmoreio deve levar em conta o gosto de quem vai degustar.

Como os animais são criados para alcançar essa qualidade?

A qualidade do Wagyu começa muito antes de a carne chegar ao açougue. A genética tem papel importante, mas o resultado também depende da alimentação, do manejo, das condições de criação e do acompanhamento da saúde dos animais.

No Japão, os criadores trabalham com linhagens selecionadas e programas específicos de alimentação, que podem incluir forragens e grãos em diferentes etapas do desenvolvimento. O objetivo é favorecer a formação gradual da gordura intramuscular, preservando a saúde dos bovinos.

A criação exige acompanhamento técnico, controle da alimentação e atenção às condições ambientais. Não existe, porém, uma única fórmula de manejo para todos os produtores. Práticas como massagens e fornecimento de cerveja, frequentemente associadas à criação de Wagyu, não são requisitos universais para produzir carne de qualidade.

No Brasil, produtores especializados também investem em genética, nutrição e rastreabilidade. É o caso da Guidara, empresa brasileira de carnes nobres que trabalha com Wagyu desde 2006. A marca seleciona geneticamente os animais, acompanha a criação e utiliza protocolos de alimentação e manejo inspirados em práticas japonesas

Quais são os melhores cortes de Wagyu para experimentar?

A escolha do corte depende do preparo e da intensidade de sabor desejada. Alguns são ideais para um jantar especial na frigideira, enquanto outros funcionam muito bem na churrasqueira.

Ancho: retirado da região dianteira do contrafilé, costuma apresentar bom marmoreio e sabor marcante. É uma ótima opção para grelhar ou preparar na churrasqueira.

Chorizo: corte da região do contrafilé, com fibras macias e sabor característico. Vai bem na grelha, com sal e poucos temperos.

Filé-mignon: conhecido pela maciez, apresenta perfil mais delicado e, em geral, menos marmoreio que cortes como ancho e chorizo. É uma alternativa para quem prefere textura suave e sabor menos intenso.

Picanha: querida no churrasco brasileiro, pode oferecer uma experiência diferente quando produzida a partir de animais Wagyu. A gordura externa e o marmoreio interno contribuem para a suculência.

Short rib: corte com osso da região das costelas, que combina carne, gordura e sabor intenso. Dependendo da espessura e do corte, pode ser preparado na grelha ou em cocção lenta.

Para uma primeira degustação, ancho e chorizo são boas escolhas. Permitem perceber a diferença de textura e sabor sem exigir técnicas complexas de preparo.

Com sabor marcante, o Wagyu pede um prato simples e delicado que ajuda a destacar as suas características. — Foto: Divulgação/Magnific.

Como preparar Wagyu sem perder suas características

Uma carne especial não precisa de uma receita complicada. Pelo contrário: o segredo está em respeitar o corte e evitar que temperos e acompanhamentos disputem a atenção com seu sabor.

Receita: Wagyu grelhado com batatas douradas e cogumelos

2 bifes de Wagyu, de aproximadamente 200 g cada

Pimenta-do-reino moída na hora, opcional

200 g de cogumelos frescos, como shiitake ou paris

Cozinhe as batatas em água com sal até ficarem macias, mas sem desmanchar. Escorra, corte ao meio e reserve.

Aqueça uma frigideira com um fio de azeite e doure as batatas com o alho e o tomilho. Deixe formar uma crosta dourada e reserve.

Na mesma frigideira, salteie os cogumelos até perderem parte da umidade e dourarem. Finalize com salsinha e uma pitada de sal.

Retire a carne da geladeira alguns minutos antes do preparo e seque a superfície com papel-toalha. Tempere com sal pouco antes de grelhar.

Aqueça bem uma frigideira pesada ou uma chapa. Coloque os bifes e doure dos dois lados, ajustando o tempo à espessura da peça e ao nível de marmoreio. Em cortes muito gordurosos, normalmente não é necessário acrescentar óleo.

Deixe a carne descansar por alguns minutos antes de servir, para que os sucos se redistribuam. Sirva com as batatas e os cogumelos.

O resultado é um prato que combina a riqueza da carne com a textura das batatas e o sabor terroso dos cogumelos, sem encobrir as características do Wagyu.

A harmonização depende do corte e do estilo da bebida. Um Wagyu muito marmorizado pede atenção especial: a gordura pode combinar com taninos, mas o excesso de madeira ou de adstringência pode tornar a experiência menos agradável.

Cabernet Sauvignon: funciona bem com cortes grelhados de sabor intenso, especialmente quando há uma crosta bem dourada. Prefira exemplares equilibrados, com taninos maduros.

Malbec argentino: é uma boa escolha para ancho, chorizo e picanha, principalmente no churrasco. Fruta madura e estrutura acompanham a intensidade da carne.

Pinot Noir: para quem prefere um tinto mais leve, pode harmonizar com Wagyu de marmoreio moderado, cogumelos e preparações menos tostadas.

Syrah: seus aromas de especiarias e frutas escuras combinam com cortes grelhados e acompanhamentos de sabor mais intenso.

Espumante brut: a acidez e as borbulhas ajudam a refrescar o paladar entre as garfadas, especialmente em preparações mais gordurosas.

Cerveja: estilos como amber ale e cervejas maltadas podem acompanhar o sabor tostado da carne. Para uma opção mais refrescante, uma lager equilibrada também funciona.

Chá verde japonês: para uma refeição inspirada na culinária do Japão, oferece uma alternativa sem álcool, com frescor e notas vegetais.

Uma regra simples é escolher uma bebida que acompanhe a intensidade do corte, sem dominá-lo. E, para a primeira experiência com Wagyu, vale provar um pequeno pedaço antes de acrescentar molhos ou combinar a carne com outros sabores.

Como comprar Wagyu de verdade e evitar falsificações

Por ser uma carne valorizada e de preço elevado, o Wagyu exige atenção na hora da compra. A popularidade do produto também faz com que seja importante verificar a procedência, a identificação da raça e as informações do fornecedor.

O primeiro cuidado é entender o que está sendo vendido. Wagyu puro, Wagyu cruzado e Wagyu japonês não são necessariamente a mesma coisa, e cada categoria pode apresentar diferenças de genética, marmoreio, origem e preço. Um produto cruzado não é automaticamente falso: o importante é que a classificação seja informada corretamente e que a procedência possa ser verificada.

No caso do Wagyu japonês, selos de autenticidade, documentação de origem e sistemas de rastreabilidade ajudam a confirmar a procedência. No Brasil, a Associação Brasileira dos Criadores de Bovinos das Raças Wagyu mantém informações sobre certificação e fornecedores de carne Wagyu certificada.

Para evitar cair em ofertas enganosas, prefira comprar em estabelecimentos que informem claramente a marca, o corte, a categoria do produto e sua origem, além de manterem as condições adequadas de refrigeração ou congelamento.

No Ítalo Supermercados, os consumidores encontram carne Wagyu da Guidara, empresa especializada em carnes nobres que mantém criação de animais da linhagem no Brasil e trabalha com rastreabilidade e seleção genética.

A escolha de um fornecedor confiável permite aproveitar melhor uma carne que reúne tradição, genética e técnica de produção. articles.title: MG é o 2º estado com mais denúncias de assédio eleitoral no trabalho | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 351 casos, número mais que triplicou desde o 1º turno, quando eram 110. Pressão pelo voto, ameaças de demissão e exigência de participação em campanhas podem caracterizar assédio.
articles.summary: Com 351 casos, número mais que triplicou desde o 1º turno, quando eram 110. Pressão pelo voto, ameaças de demissão e exigência de participação em campanhas podem caracterizar assédio.
articles.body:
Minas Gerais chegou a 351 denúncias de assédio eleitoral em 2026, segundo dados divulgados pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) até as 10h desta quinta-feira (29). O estado tem o segundo maior número de registros do país , atrás apenas de São Paulo, que soma 620.

O avanço dos casos em MG se intensificou durante o pleito e continuou mesmo depois da votação. Veja:

Ao fim do primeiro turno, em 4 de outubro, eram 110 registros.

No encerramento do segundo turno, no último domingo (25), o número havia subido para 212.

Agora, as denúncias chegaram a 351 — mais do que o triplo do registrado no primeiro turno.

O aumento ocorre em meio a uma nova onda de publicações nas redes sociais que incentivam a demissão e a recusa de contratação de profissionais por preferência política , além de promover listas de boicote a empresas supostamente apoiadoras do presidente reeleito Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Em resposta, o ministro do Trabalho e Emprego, Luiz Marinho, anunciou na quarta-feira (28) uma força-tarefa nacional para fiscalizar denúncias de ameaças de demissão , perseguição e outras formas de assédio eleitoral contra trabalhadores.

🔍 O assédio eleitoral no trabalho ocorre quando o empregador tenta influenciar o voto do funcionário por meio de ameaças, como perda do emprego, redução salarial ou rebaixamento de cargo, ou promove atividades políticas, como distribuição de santinhos e eventos, no ambiente de trabalho ( leia mais abaixo ) .

Durante as eleições, o Ministério Público do Trabalho em Minas Gerais adotou medidas para tentar impedir pressões sobre trabalhadores. Até o encerramento do segundo turno, o órgão havia expedido 118 recomendações a empregadores e recorrido à Justiça do Trabalho em sete casos considerados mais graves.

Em Bom Despacho, no Centro-Oeste de Minas, por exemplo, o MPT ajuizou uma ação após receber denúncia sobre a realização de um ato de campanha dentro de uma fábrica de calçados. A Justiça determinou a interrupção de atividades político-eleitorais no estabelecimento e a adoção de medidas para conscientizar os funcionários sobre o voto livre e secreto.

Também houve atuação do MPT contra uma siderúrgica de Monsenhor Paulo, no Sul de Minas, investigada por indícios de uso do ambiente de trabalho para influenciar as escolhas políticas dos empregados.

No país, o MPT contabilizou 3.396 denúncias em 2026 até as 10h desta quinta . O número já ultrapassa o registrado nas eleições de 2022, quando foram mais de 3.373 ocorrências.

Somente em outubro, foram cerca de 2,6 mil denúncias no Brasil, alta de aproximadamente 371% em relação a setembro, quando houve 552 registros. O volume deste mês corresponde a cerca de 77% de todas as denúncias contabilizadas no ano até agora.

São Paulo aparece em primeiro lugar, com 620 denúncias, seguido por Minas Gerais, com 351, e Rio de Janeiro, com 252 ( veja infográfico e mapa abaixo ).

🔍 O painel usado para contabilizar as denúncias é dinâmico. Por isso, os números podem mudar à medida que novos relatos são recebidos e cadastrados .

Denúncias de assédio eleitoral no trabalho em 2026 por estado — Foto: Arte g1

Para que mais casos cheguem às autoridades, o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) está enviando mensagens pela Carteira de Trabalho Digital para incentivar trabalhadores a denunciar situações de assédio eleitoral no ambiente profissional.

A mensagem alerta para ameaças de demissão e discriminação política relacionadas ao voto. O texto diz: “Você sofreu ameaça de demissão ou discriminação política no trabalho? O Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego existe para te proteger. Denuncie o assédio aqui:

Print de mensagem do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) sobre assédio eleitoral — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O assédio eleitoral no trabalho ocorre quando empregadores, gestores ou outras pessoas tentam constranger, pressionar ou influenciar um trabalhador a votar, apoiar ou manifestar preferência por determinado candidato, partido político ou posição ideológica.

Por exemplo, a prática pode ocorrer por meio de ameaças de demissão, rebaixamento de cargo ou redução salarial caso o empregado vote em determinado candidato.

Também pode envolver a distribuição de material de campanha ou a realização de eventos políticos no ambiente de trabalho, especialmente quando há pressão ou constrangimento dos trabalhadores.

A prática é definida pela Resolução CSJT nº 355/2023, da Justiça do Trabalho. Entre as condutas que podem caracterizar assédio estão coação, intimidação, ameaça, humilhação e outras formas de constrangimento usadas para interferir na escolha política ou no direito ao voto livre e secreto.

Também pode haver assédio quando o trabalhador recebe tratamento diferente por causa de sua opinião ou convicção política, como exclusão, favorecimento ou discriminação no ambiente de trabalho, inclusive em processos seletivos e de contratação.

Para as eleições de 2026, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) editou a Resolução nº 23.755/2026, que incluiu o § 2º-A no artigo 19 da Resolução nº 23.610/2019.

A norma passou a proibir expressamente a propaganda eleitoral e o assédio eleitoral em ambientes de trabalho públicos e privados, responsabilizando quem pratica ou permite essas condutas.

Em agosto, o TSE, a Justiça do Trabalho, o Ministério Público Eleitoral (MPE) e o MPT também firmaram um acordo de cooperação técnica para reforçar ações de prevenção, fiscalização e combate ao assédio eleitoral.

Entre as situações que podem caracterizar assédio eleitoral estão:

ameaçar demitir quem não votar em determinado candidato;

prometer aumento salarial, benefício ou outra vantagem em troca de voto;

exigir participação em campanha eleitoral;

distribuir material de campanha e pressionar os empregados a utilizá-lo;

cobrar o voto ou tentar descobrir em quem o trabalhador votará;

retaliar quem manifesta preferência política diferente da do empregador;

impor o uso de símbolos, roupas ou materiais de campanha.

articles.title: Incêndio em Lagarto atinge veículos e depósito no Povoado Barragem | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo atingiu a área externa de um imóvel usado como depósito no Povoado Barragem; não houve feridos.
articles.summary: Incêndio em Lagarto mobilizou bombeiros e consumiu 5 mil litros de água para apagar chamas que atingiram veículos e pneus em um depósito no Povoado Barragem.
articles.body:
Um incêndio em vegetação se alastrou e atingiu veículos e outros materiais guardados na área externa de uma residência no Povoado Barragem, em Lagarto , no Centro-Sul sergipano. A informação foi divulgada na tarde desta quinta-feira (29).

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar de Sergipe (CBMSE), o imóvel atingido, nesta quarta-feira, funcionava como depósito . A presença de pneus, três veículos e diversos eletrodomésticos em desuso no quintal facilitou a rápida propagação das chamas. Ninguém se feriu.

Para conter o fogo, a equipe precisou desligar a rede elétrica do local e utilizar cerca de 5 mil litros de água. A operação durou aproximadamente uma hora e meia e contou com uma fase de rescaldo para evitar o surgimento de novos focos.

articles.title: Oregon’s 1989 dam diverted water to one landowner’s pond; its 2020 removal kept his water right via a pump and reopened 1.8 miles of creek for coho salmon
articles.summary: The removal of a 1989 dam on Kelley Creek, Oregon, has restored migratory paths for coho salmon and maintained water rights for a local landowner through pump technology. This environmental restoration project opens 1.8 miles of vital habitat, promoting biodiversity and sustainable land use.
articles.body: A dam built across Kelley Creek in 1989 in Oregon blocked migrating fish from reaching upstream habitat for three decades while diverting water into a private owner’s pond. The structure was nearly six feet tall, and it reportedly obstructed fish passage through the lower part of the creek, a tributary within the Johnson Creek watershed near Portland. In August 2020, the Johnson Creek Watershed Council (JCWC) removed the dam and substituted its gravity-fed water diversion with a pump, thus allowing the landowner to continue using his water right. 1.8 miles of accessible habitat as the project’s target was identified by the Clackamas Partnership. This was intended to be an opening route that would benefit coho salmon, steelhead and Pacific lamprey. Subsequent environmental DNA observation detected coho salmon at the former dam site, thus providing evidence of their presence extending beyond the barrier.A dam that blocked fish passage for three decadesThe dam was built at river mile 0.5 on Kelley Creek with the intention of holding water upstream and feeding a gravity-powered diversion into an off-channel pond. While the structure served the estateowner’s water needs, the structure spanned the creek and prevented fish like salmon, steelhead and lamprey from migrating into upstream habitat. The Clackamas Partnership classified this as a complete barrier to salmonid passage. Kelley Creek and its tributaries include habitat used by migratory fish, which made the obstruction a priority for restoration efforts in the wider Johnson Creek watershed.In 2015, the planning for fish-passage improvements began. Following this, in 2017, JCWC secured funding from the East Multnomah Soil and Water Conservation District, allowing consultants to explore options for bettering the passage. A 60% engineering design was reportedly completed in November 2018. The team initially considered ways to construct a route that fish could use to bypass the structure. However, when presented with the alternatives, the landowner reportedly suggested removing the dam altogether. That proposal moved the project towards eliminating the barrier while preserving the pond’s water supply.Meanwhile, engineers designed a submersible pump station downstream of the former barrier, near the pond, to replace the gravity-fed diversion. The Clackamas Partnership reported that the Oregon Water Resources Department approved a formal amendment to the water right’s point of diversion and waived the associated processing fee. This pump provided the means of physically drawing water. Therefore, the dam could be removed without requiring the landowner to abandon the existing water use.Removing the barrier and restoring the channelIn August 2020, the removal of the dam was finished. Prior to the demolition, teams slowly lowered the impounded water, exposing mudflats and giving Pacific lamprey buried in the sediment an opportunity to emerge so they could be captured and relocated. This gradual drawdown was aimed at reducing harm to aquatic life during construction. Following the dam’s removal, engineers installed an engineered streambed in the former structure’s footprint to reduce the risk of the channel eroding downwards or cutting sideways into its banks.The replacement water-diversion system also required some changes to the stream channel. Engineers built a riffle downstream to help maintain the pool needed for the pump intake. A screened intake was installed to lessen the risk of fish being drawn into the diversion, while a boulder weir helped direct the flow towards the centre of the pool and keep the screen clear of debris. These features allowed water withdrawal to continue without recreating the original barrier to fish migration.Furthermore, the restoration work included measures to protect the creek beyond the former dam site. According to JCWC, a fence along the stream to prevent livestock from entering the channel was installed alongside plans for riparian revegetation. The department believed that keeping livestock away from the creek can help protect streambanks and newly planted vegetation from trampling. Together, the channel reconstruction and streamside protection measures were intended to improve the stability of the restored reach and support its use by aquatic species.Beyond the former barrier, coho salmon were detectedThe project’s targeted performance measure listed 1.8 miles of accessible stream habitat along Kelley Creek. Its fact sheet identifies coho salmon, steelhead and Pacific lamprey as focal species. In a separate JCWC project documentation in 2020, it was reported that fish passage had been restored to a cumulative total of nearly three miles of Kelley and Mitchell creeks.Subsequent monitoring showed that coho salmon were present at the former dam site. The council’s environmental DNA programme, which analyses genetic material collected from stream water, reported coho salmon DNA at the site where the dam had been removed. articles.title: Pensioners, you can submit your life certificate from home: Who can apply, how it works and the November 30 deadline
articles.summary: Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive.
articles.body: Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive. They can generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home on a smartphone, using the government’s Jeevan Pramaan facility. The service lets pensioners submit their annual life certificate electronically, using Aadhaar-based face authentication without visiting a bank branch. The yearly certificate is what keeps pension payments from being interrupted.Dates and deadline for 2026Presioners who are 80 years old and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November 30, 2026. On the other hand, those below 80 years if age canPensioners aged 80 and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November submit it from November 1 to November 30. With the November window about to open for most pensioners, anyone who has not yet submitted should plan to do it early and not leave it to the last weekWhat you needFor face authentication, pensioners need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera. They must download two apps, AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App. The sources I found describe the process only for Android phones, so iPhone users should check the official Jeevan Pramaan website for their options.The process is also tied to Aadhaar. As per the State Bank of India, the submission of life certificate is an Aadhaar-based process as it helps in the digital authentication and it works only if the account of the pensioner is seeded with their Aadhar number. Before starting the process, the pensioners should check whether their Aadhaar card is linked to their pension account and that the mobile number registered with Aadhaar is active, as the process also requires OTP.How it worksThe steps vary slightly by app version, but the general flow is simple.1. Check your Aadhaar links. The digital life certificate can be authenticated only if your pension account is seeded with your Aadhaar number, and keep your Aadhaar-registered mobile number active for the OTP.2. Use a compatible phone. You need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera.3. Download the two apps. Install AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App.4. Open the Jeevan Pramaan app and register. Enter your Aadhaar number and mobile number, then verify with the OTP.5. Fill in your pension details. These include pensioner type, PPO number, bank and disbursing agency.6. Complete face authentication. Capture your face with the phone’s front camera and follow the on-screen instructions.7. Save your Pramaan ID. A unique ID is generated once the process succeeds. You will also get an SMS with a transaction ID.8. Download your certificate. Use the transaction ID at jeevanpramaan.gov.in to download the computer-generated certificate for your records.9. Confirm it was accepted. A successful face scan doesn’t necessarily mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate, so check with your bank or disbursing agency before November 30.Submission is not the same as acceptanceAn important caution is that a successful face scan does not automatically mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate. Business Standard notes that pensioners should visit the Jeevan Pramaan portal after submission and use the Pramaan ID to access their certificate. Pensioners should also keep the ID and SMS, and check with their bank or disbursing agency that the certificate has been recorded before the deadline.If you can’t use a smartphoneNot everyone is comfortable with apps. SBI says a physical life certificate will continue to be accepted if the pensioner prefers it. Other routes include fingerprint or iris devices, the UMANG app, and help at banks, post offices and Common Service Centres. Government campaigns have also run special camps through pension disbursing banks and India Post Payments Bank, and traditional methods remain available for those who cannot access the digital platform. articles.body: Streamer Vitaly has been suspended from Kick after the platform accused him of breaking its rules on endangerment. articles.title: ‘This is the future you want?’ White House cites France riots to warn against Democrats ahead of midterms
articles.summary: The White House on Thursday shared a video of violent protest scenes from France, claiming that the unrest could represent their future if they back the
articles.body: The White House on Thursday shared a video of violent protest scenes from France, claiming that the unrest could represent their future if they back the Democratic Party in the November 3 midterm elections.“France before and after is a warning. The chaos, looting, and destruction we’re watching is exactly the future radical Democrats are pushing for America. Is this the future you want?” the White House wrote in a post on X.The post comes amid some of France’s worst unrest in decades, with demonstrations over rising living costs, inequality and deteriorating public services escalating into violence in several cities. The Trump administration has seized on the scenes to criticise immigration policies and portray Democrats as a threat to law and order.France’s protests, however, began with grievances over the country’s education system, including teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and poor school facilities, before expanding into wider economic and political discontent. While hundreds of thousands of people took part in demonstrations, violent groups looted shops, attacked police and set buildings and vehicles on fire.What is happening in France?The unrest gathered momentum in September, beginning with student demonstrations over staff shortages and conditions in schools before drawing in teachers, parents, trade unions and other protesters angry about living costs and public spending. The movement also brought together groups opposed to the government’s economic policies, including supporters of the Yellow Vest movement that staged mass protests in 2018.The violence escalated on October 17, when an estimated 550,000 to 800,000 people took part in demonstrations across France. Although most marches were peaceful, some groups looted shops, attacked police and damaged public buildings. Limoges city hall was set on fire, while protesters broke into Marseille city hall and a tourist office in Lyon was torched. Authorities reported around 1,200 arrests and more than 150 injured police officers.What Trump has said on the unrestThe White House’s post follows President Donald Trump’s repeated attempts to link the French unrest to immigration and left-wing politics. A video published by the White House on October 23 combined footage of violence in France with excerpts from Trump’s speech at a rally in Kansas, where he blamed migrants and other groups for the country’s turmoil.The messaging comes just days before the US midterm elections, in which control of Congress is at stake. Trump and other Republicans have invoked the French unrest to argue that Democratic policies could lead to similar disorder in the United States. However, reports on the protests identify school conditions, the cost of living, inequality and public services among the movement’s central grievances, while the violence was concentrated among some groups participating in the wider demonstrations.You use AI every day. articles.title: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum donated $36 million to help establish a Los Angeles school campus; on October 25, the new campus opened for grades 9–12, bringing the school's total footprint to 28 acres
articles.summary: A $36 million donation from WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum has helped a Jewish school in Los Angeles expand its facilities, with a new campus opening for
articles.body: A $36 million donation from WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum has helped a Jewish school in Los Angeles expand its facilities, with a new campus opening for high school students on Sunday. Milken Community School, which teaches students from grades 6 to 12, has moved its upper school students to the Jan Koum Campus in Bel Air. With the addition of this property, the school now has 28 acres of land spread across three campuses.According to Jewish Journal, the new campus stands at 15600 Mulholland Drive, a property that previously belonged to American Jewish University. It is about half a mile from Milken's two other campuses, known as the Ruby Family Campus and Saperstein Campus. Stephen Wise Temple is located across the street.The school marked the opening with a gathering of families, students, donors and community leaders. According to the Jewish Journal, Israeli singer Ishay Ribo performed at the event, his first appearance before the Milken community. Ribo was the first Israeli artist to headline a concert at Madison Square Garden.WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum was born on February 24, 1976, into a Jewish family in Kyiv, Ukraine. When he was 16, he moved to California with his mother and grandmother to escape antisemitism and religious persecution in the former Soviet Union.A June 15, 2022, investigation by the Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that his foundation had donated millions of dollars to Jewish organisations, including approximately $17 million to the European Jewish Association during 2019–2020. The report also noted that Koum had maintained a relatively low public profile regarding his Jewish identity, despite his substantial financial support for Jewish causes.The $36 million donation The property was not always called the Jan Koum Campus. After Milken School co-founder and trustee Lowell Milken acquired it from American Jewish University, it was known as Milken East Campus. The name changed in June 2026, when the school announced a major contribution from the Koum Family Foundation.In a June 18 announcement, Shulkind confirmed that the foundation had committed $36 million towards the school's expansion. The contribution increased the total collected through Milken's capital campaign to $152 million. The school said the fundraising amount was a record in Jewish education.According to Milken Community School's official website, the Koum Family Foundation supports Jewish education and identity-building, works to strengthen the State of Israel and serves Jewish communities around the world. articles.body: US President Donald Trump made a risky joke that the $5,000 payment he has promised Americans would barely cover a hamburger and a small dessert at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, surprisingly drawing laughter and applause from supporters at a campaign rally in Texas.Trump made the remarks at a rally in Corpus Christi on Tuesday, urging supporters to spend the money in the United States rather than overseas. His comments came as the rising cost of living has emerged as a key issue ahead of the November 3 congressional elections. PTI reported.“Go to Florida, go to any one of our great places,” Trump said. “You could even come to Mar-a-Lago. I said it the other night. You’ll be my guest at Mar-a-Lago. The problem is that for USD 5,000, the most you’ll be able to buy is a hamburger and maybe a small dessert. I’m not even sure you could buy that. No, don’t go there. That’s not a good place if you’re price conscious.”The audience, however, responded with laughter and applause rather than taking offence at the joke, suggesting the loyal Maga base the President enjoys.The remarks came amid concerns over affordability, an issue that analysts say could affect the Republicans’ position in Congress.Trump has promised to send cheques worth $5,000 to every American adult if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress. The proposal has drawn criticism from Democrats and some supporters of the president, with critics questioning its feasibility and describing it as an attempt to influence voters.The estimated cost of the payments would be USD 1.3 trillion, according to the supplied estimate reported by PTI, and implementing the proposal would require congressional action.The elections on November 3 will determine all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate. Together, the two chambers make up the US Congress, where Republicans currently hold majorities in both.Congressional elections take place every two years. One coincides with the four-year presidential election, while the other is held midway through a president’s term.Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate. Of the 35 seats up for election, Republicans hold 22 and Democrats hold 13. Democrats would need to retain their 13 seats and win four additional seats to secure a majority.In the House of Representatives, Republicans hold 218 seats and Democrats 214, while one seat belongs to an independent. Two seats are vacant.Beyond the congressional races, voters will also elect governors in 36 states. In Ohio, a Republican stronghold, Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is facing Democrat Amy Acton in a closely watched contest.A recent Pew Research Centre study, quoted by PTI, found that 60 per cent of Americans said they did not have enough income to live the life they wanted, while 70 per cent said they had cut back on discretionary spending, including eating out.Trump has continued to maintain that the US economy is performing well and has dismissed concerns about affordability as an issue invented by Democrats.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump moves to end H-1B visa deference: What it means for Indians stuck in the green-card backlog
articles.summary: For Indian professionals working in the US, an H-1B extension is more than a routine immigration formality.
articles.body: For Indian professionals working in the US, an H-1B extension is more than a routine immigration formality. It is a crucial bridge to maintaining legal status and keeping their path to permanent residency, or a green card, alive as they navigate a backlog that can stretch for decades.Many rely on successive extensions while waiting for their employment-based green cards. A proposed change by the Trump administration could make that process more uncertain, even for workers whose previous visa petitions were approved.The administration has proposed scrapping the US immigration policy known as “deference to prior approvals”. Under the policy, US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) generally gives weight to an earlier favourable decision when reviewing an extension petition involving the same employer, worker and underlying facts, unless certain exceptions apply.The policy requires immigration officers to consider previous approvals, while the proposed change could make it easier for them to reassess a worker’s eligibility.The proposal, published on October 14, is not yet a final rule. If implemented, it could mean closer scrutiny of extension applications from Indian H-1B holders, including those who have spent years building their lives and careers in the US while waiting for employment-based green cards.The change could also affect workers in other visa categories, including L-1 intracompany transfers.Rajiv Dabhadkar, founder of the National Organisation for Software and Technology Professionals (NOSTOPS), told TOI,“Removing deference would not itself change green card queue positions or automatically invalidate existing H-1B approvals. However, it could affect how subsequent petitions are assessed while individuals wait for permanent residency.”Immigration attorney Bhumireddy Sai Srinivas Reddy told TOI the proposal could make the long wait for permanent residency more uncertain for Indian H-1B holders.“For Indian H-1B holders in the EB-2/EB-3 backlog, this rule changes the nature of the green-card wait itself. Most are living on three-year AC21 extensions, four, five, six renewals over a decade. Today each renewal presumes the last approval was correct. Under the proposed rule, every renewal becomes a fresh trial of eligibility, with specialty occupation, wage level, and employer relationship all back on the table,” he said.Indians accounted for about 70 per cent of all H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal year 2025, according to USCIS data, making them a significant group potentially affected by any change to how work visa extensions are adjudicated.What is the US deference policy, and what could change?The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and USCIS have proposed removing a provision under 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which generally requires the agency to give “deference to a prior approval” when adjudicating a request to extend a non-immigrant worker's petition involving the same parties and underlying facts.The DHS explains: “When adjudicating a request filed on Form I-129 (Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker) involving the same parties and the same underlying facts, USCIS gives deference to its prior determination of the petitioner's, applicant's, or beneficiary's eligibility.”However, deference is not an unconditional guarantee of approval.Under the existing regulation, USCIS can depart from an earlier determination if there was a material error, a material change or new material information that adversely affects eligibility.Employers use Form I-129 to petition for foreign workers in several temporary employment categories, including H-1B, L-1, O-1 and other non-immigrant classifications.If the proposal is finalised, USCIS officers would still be able to consider previous approvals where relevant. However, they would no longer be required to begin from a position of deference to an earlier decision.The proposed change would therefore alter the framework for reviewing extension petitions, rather than automatically changing the basic eligibility requirements for each visa category.How could this affect Indian H-1B professionals waiting for green cards?The proposed change could be particularly consequential for Indian professionals who have spent years working in the US while waiting for employment-based green cards.The H-1B visa allows US employers to hire foreign workers in specialised occupations, with an annual cap of 65,000 visas and another 20,000 for qualifying US advanced-degree graduates.It is generally granted for up to three years and can be extended for another three, with certain workers eligible for extensions beyond the usual six-year limit while pursuing employment-based green cards.For many Indian professionals, the green-card process can stretch over decades because of the high demand for employment-based immigrant visas and country-specific limits on their allocation.A recent analysis by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) estimated that nearly one million Indians are stuck in the US employment-based green-card backlog, accounting for close to 79 per cent of the estimated 1.26 million people waiting in the first three employment-based preference categories.The NFAP analysis also estimated that an Indian professional entering the queue in 2026 could face a potential wait of 179 years in the EB-2 category and 38 years in EB-3, under its modelling assumptions.These projections show the scale of the backlog, although actual waiting periods depend on factors such as visa availability, category and priority date, as well as future policy changes.This would not automatically mean denials, but could increase documentation requirements and uncertainty over processing times.Dabhadkar said, “Additional scrutiny could mean more evidence requests, higher legal and administrative costs, and uncertainty over continued employment, affecting workers’ career decisions and long-term planning.”More scrutiny, additional paperwork for employers?If USCIS officers seek additional evidence, employers may have to submit more detailed documentation relating to job duties, compensation, work locations, business operations, contracts and workers' qualifications.Employers may also need to demonstrate that workers continue to meet the eligibility requirements of their respective visa categories, rather than relying heavily on the fact that an earlier petition was approved.An analysis by the Vasquez Law Firm said the proposal could change how USCIS reviews subsequent petitions.“A worker may feel the practical effects even though the employer is often the petitioner,” the firm noted, explaining that employers may have to document the offered role, business operations, compensation, contracts, work location and the worker's qualifications again.The firm also said workers may need records showing that they have continued to maintain their non-immigrant status.DHS estimates that the proposed rule would impose nearly $133,987 in additional annual costs on petitioners and lead to around 6,044 additional requests for evidence (RFEs) each year.The department says the change could increase adjudication workloads and operational costs as officers spend more time reassessing eligibility and reviewing additional evidence.Reddy said delays caused by additional evidence requests could have consequences for workers whose employment authorisation depends on timely decisions.“The real risk is delay, not denial. More RFEs mean more petitions pending past the 240-day work-authorization window and a worker who hits day 241 must stop working, even with an approved I-140 and a decade of lawful status. With automatic EAD extensions gone, an H-4 spouse's work authorization can lapse in the same queue,” he said.For employers, the consequences could include greater legal and administrative expenses, more time spent preparing extension petitions and less certainty in workforce planning. For workers, additional requests for evidence could prolong the decision-making process.Why does the Trump administration want to end deference?The Trump administration argues that the existing policy could limit the ability of immigration officers to examine applications independently.In its proposal, the DHS said the deference policy may have resulted in “perpetuating erroneous prior approvals and creating an environment in which fraudulent and meritless petitions are less likely to be detected before approval”.The department also argued that some employers may have interpreted the policy as reducing their obligation to show that a worker continues to meet the requirements of the requested visa classification.According to the proposal, the existing regulation effectively shifts the burden from the petitioner to the USCIS officer, who must justify departing from an earlier approval.The DHS says removing the requirement would better align its regulations and adjudication practices with its interpretation of the Immigration and Nationality Act, under which the burden of establishing eligibility for immigration benefits rests with the petitioner.“Removing the deference requirement would also help to ensure that USCIS officers fully review the facts and evidence in every case to ensure continued eligibility,” the proposal states.The policy has changed several times over the years. USCIS first issued guidance on deference in 2004, rescinded it in 2017, and reinstated it in its Policy Manual in 2021. The DHS formally codified the policy in December 2024. The latest proposal would reverse that codification.What happens next?The proposal is open for public comments until November 13, 2026. Interested parties can submit feedback through the federal rulemaking portal, citing DHS Docket No. USCIS-2026-0529.Employers, immigration attorneys, and other stakeholders can use the consultation period to raise concerns about the potential impact on workers and businesses.For Indian professionals, the proposal would change how extension petitions are reviewed, not H-1B eligibility requirements or the existing six-year limit. Current rules remain in effect until a final rule is published and takes effect.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: At 26, Kia Humberstone began building a $40,000 home on a truck to avoid a traditional mortgage after selling her first tiny home for A$35,000, seeking a more affordable path to homeownership
articles.summary: At 26, Kia Humberstone began building a home on the back of a vintage truck and trailer, hoping to find a more affordable path to homeownership without
articles.body: At 26, Kia Humberstone began building a home on the back of a vintage truck and trailer, hoping to find a more affordable path to homeownership without committing to decades of mortgage repayments. Based in Margaret River, Western Australia, she estimated that her second tiny-home project would cost around A$40,000, using recycled materials and her own labour to keep expenses down. Her decision followed an earlier experiment in unconventional living: during the COVID-19 pandemic, she built a tiny home on a truck for A$12,000, lived in it rent-free for two years and later sold it for A$35,000. She used the proceeds to fund a two-year camping trip around Australia. Now, she is building another mobile dwelling to create a home base while retaining the freedom to travel.Why Kia Humberstone chose an alternative to a traditional mortgageHumberstone returned to Margaret River after spending nine months in Sydney, where she became dissatisfied with city life. Having grown up in the countryside, she wanted to return to a simpler lifestyle but found that securing affordable housing remained difficult.She was concerned that taking out a conventional home loan as a single person could leave her making repayments well into retirement. Rather than commit to a mortgage, she decided to build a home herself, aiming to gain greater financial independence and flexibility.Her project reflects a personal response to Australia's housing affordability challenges, particularly for younger people who find it difficult to buy property or secure suitable rental accommodation. Rather than purchasing a conventional house, Humberstone chose to build a mobile dwelling that could serve as her home without being permanently tied to a block of land.She bought a 1988 Isuzu truck for A$5,000For her latest project, Humberstone purchased a 1988 Isuzu truck and trailer for A$5,000. She is converting the vehicle into an approximately 13-metre tiny home, with a projected total cost of around A$40,000.The restoration proved more demanding than she had initially expected. After cleaning the truck, she discovered extensive rust that needed to be removed and treated before construction could progress.Her work included grinding away corrosion, treating the metal, patching holes with fibreglass and sanding the surface in preparation for painting. She was also working towards giving the vehicle a glossy green finish.Once the restoration was complete, the next stage involved installing the walls that would divide the interior into separate living spaces. The project required considerable hands-on work, with Humberstone undertaking much of the labour herself to keep costs manageable.What the A$40,000 tiny home will includeHumberstone planned to turn the truck and trailer into a functional dwelling with four essential areas: a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen and lounge room.The design aims to provide the basic comforts of a conventional home within a compact, mobile structure. Recycled materials are expected to help reduce the overall expenditure, while doing much of the construction herself allows her to avoid some labour costs.At the time of the February 2026 reports, the home was still under construction. Humberstone hoped to move in with the essentials within approximately two months, although she expected the complete project to take another year.The A$40,000 figure is her estimated budget rather than a confirmed final cost. The reports did not establish that the build was completed within that amount.Her first tiny home cost A$12,000 and sold for A$35,000Humberstone had already experimented with truck-based housing during the COVID-19 pandemic, when she built her first tiny home on her parents' property using recycled materials.That project cost approximately A$12,000 and provided her with a place to live without paying rent for two years. She subsequently sold the dwelling for A$35,000, more than twice her original investment.Humberstone used the proceeds to finance a two-year camping trip around Australia. The experience gave her an opportunity to travel while demonstrating how a relatively low-cost housing project could support her preferred lifestyle.Her latest build follows a similar idea, but she intends to create a home base that she can return to between trips. The first project also gave her practical experience of building a dwelling from reused materials and managing a construction project on a limited budget.She is working three jobs to finance the buildHumberstone is funding the new home by working three jobs while carrying out much of the restoration and construction herself. She is also using recyclable materials wherever possible to keep expenses down.The approach demands considerable time and physical effort, from repairing the truck to preparing it for its conversion into a dwelling. Her experience with the first tiny home has given her a starting point, although the second project involves a larger vehicle and an estimated budget of A$40,000.Rather than buying a completed tiny home, she is building one from the vehicle up. This allows her to control the design and work at a pace that fits her available finances, although the final cost will depend on the work and materials required to finish it.Why she chose to build a home on wheelsOne of Humberstone's main reasons for choosing a truck was that she did not own land. A mobile dwelling would give her a place to live without first having to purchase a block of property.She also said that building on a truck offered an alternative to a permanent structure, which she believed would avoid certain council regulations. That is her stated reasoning, rather than confirmation that mobile homes are exempt from planning, parking or other legal requirements in every location.The truck format also fits her plans to continue travelling. Once completed, the dwelling is intended to provide a home base without requiring her to give up the flexibility that has shaped her lifestyle.For Humberstone, the objective is not to replicate a conventional house at a lower price, but to find a way of owning a home that better suits her finances and priorities.Her plan is to live in the home before travelling overseasHumberstone said she hoped to live in the new dwelling for about a year, enjoy the results of her work and potentially rent it out before travelling overseas.She has described the truck home as her future “little home base”, giving her somewhere to return to while continuing to explore other places.The plan combines a relatively low-cost living arrangement with the possibility of generating rental income when she is away. However, the reports describe her intentions at the time of publication and do not confirm whether she subsequently completed the build, moved in or rented out the home.For now, the project represents her attempt to balance homeownership with a lifestyle that leaves room for travel, rather than committing to a conventional mortgage and a fixed property.She hopes to inspire other young people to consider alternative homeownershipHumberstone has been sharing updates about the construction on social media, hoping to encourage other young people, particularly women, to explore alternative routes to homeownership.Her message is that owning a home does not necessarily have to follow the conventional path of purchasing a house with a long-term mortgage. Her own experience includes building a low-cost tiny home, living in it rent-free and selling it to finance travel.Her approach will not suit everyone, and a truck-based dwelling still involves expenses and practical considerations such as where it can be parked, access to utilities, sanitation, insurance and relevant local rules. Nevertheless, her project offers an example of how someone is adapting their housing plans to fit their financial circumstances and preferred way of life.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, 29 October 2026, and the Moon spends the whole day in Gemini.
articles.body: Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, 29 October 2026, and the Moon spends the whole day in Gemini. Fasting women will wait for a waning Moon that is quick, talkative and restless by nature. Gemini is an air sign ruled by Mercury. It favours news, short trips, letters, deals and second thoughts.This year the picture has an extra edge. Uranus, the planet of surprises, is also sitting in Gemini, so the Moon passes very close to it in these hours. Mercury is retrograde in Scorpio. Venus is retrograde too, at the end of Libra. And Mars and Jupiter are moving together through Leo, with the Moon forming a friendly sextile to both. Put simply, the day can bring unexpected openings, though plans may need a second look before they are locked.Six signs feel this shift more strongly than the rest.GeminiThe Moon in your own sign puts you at the centre of attention. A message, a call back or a fresh offer may arrive without warning. Uranus nearby makes you want to act at once. But Mercury, your ruler, is retrograde, so read the fine print twice. Married Geminis may find the evening rituals unusually emotional. A small gesture from a partner can mean more than any gift.LeoFor Leo, the Moon lights up the area of friends, gains and long-held wishes. With Jupiter and Mars both in your sign, support from your circle can turn into something useful. An old contact may suddenly remember you. So keep your phone close. Money matters look brighter than they have in weeks, though big spending should wait until Mercury moves direct.LibraVenus, your ruling planet, is retrograde in your sign, and that has kept some things on hold. Today the Moon forms a soft trine to Venus. Talks that stalled can restart. A delayed travel plan or a pending reply from abroad may finally move. Couples could rediscover an old warmth. Don’t force a decision on property or joint funds, though. Let it settle for a few days.AquariusThe Moon moves through your fifth house of love, children and creative work. Expect a surprise in matters of the heart. Single Aquarians may hear from someone they had almost forgotten. Parents might get good news about a child’s studies or plans. And creative projects get a sudden push. Pluto in your sign adds depth, so feelings that come up today are worth taking seriously.AriesSaturn is retrograde in Aries and has made recent weeks feel heavy. The Gemini Moon gives you a lighter, faster energy. Short travel, paperwork and conversations with siblings carry luck. A quick idea can solve a problem that has dragged on. Speak clearly and avoid sharp words in the evening. Patience pays off better than force right now.VirgoGemini touches your career zone, and Mercury rules both signs. A sudden change at work is possible. It could be a new responsibility, an unexpected meeting or praise from a senior. Some Virgos may get an offer that seemed out of reach. Still, Mercury retrograde suggests checking every detail before saying yes. At home, a quiet word of thanks to elders brings peace.What This Means for EveryoneThe Moon in Gemini makes minds busy on a day that asks for stillness. Fasting can feel tiring when thoughts keep racing. Short prayers, slow breathing and a little silence before moonrise help. Because Venus and Mercury are both retrograde, it’s a better day to repair bonds than to start brand-new commitments. A forgotten promise kept tonight can do more good than a new one made.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Reliance Jio takes biggest share with 1.9 million as India adds 2.2 million subscribers in September
articles.summary: Reliance Jio continued its dominant run across India’s telecommunications sector in September, adding up 1.9 million mobile subscribers (excluding
articles.body: Reliance Jio continued its dominant run across India’s telecommunications sector in September, adding up 1.9 million mobile subscribers (excluding machine-to-machine connections) and capturing the lion’s share of the industry's monthly growth. According to Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) data analysed by brokerages DAM Capital and IIFL Capital, the Indian telecom sector added a net total of 2.2 million mobile subscribers during the month. The expansion lifted the nation’s total wireless subscriber base (excluding M2M connections) to 1.155 billion, marking a year-on-year addition of 22.8 million users.Jio pulls ahead Airtel and ViJio’s September performance mirrored its August numbers. The telecom giant added 1.9 million core mobile users, taking its total mobile base to approximately 483 million. On an annual basis, Jio has added 17.4 million users.For Bharti Airtel, net additions dropped to 200,000, bringing its total mobile base to 406 million. Its year-on-year growth stood at 13.3 million. Vodafone Idea (Vi) continued to bleed users, with underlying losses widening to 300,000 (260,000 based on IIFL Capital's specific breakdown) compared to a loss of 140,000 in August.State-run BSNL maintained positive momentum, adding roughly 500,000 mobile subscribers for the second consecutive month, cushioning Vi's losses and lifting total industry tallies.Jio vs Airtel vs Vi: Active subscriber gainsThe gap between operators grew even more apparent in Visitor Location Register (VLR) data, which measures active network connections. Jio gained 1.3 million active VLR subscribers during September; in contrast, Airtel shed 200,000 active users, while Vodafone Idea lost 300,000. Across the entire telecom landscape, the core VLR base expanded by 600,000.When it comes to wired and fixed-broadband, Jio also outpaced Airtel, adding roughly 400,000 connections in September compared to Airtel’s 200,000. India's total home broadband base grew by 600,000 to reach 68.1 million users, though both operators experienced a mild slowdown from the monthly additions of over one million recorded in prior periods.You use AI every day.
