articles.title: Running outside when it’s dark out requires extra safety precautions — here’s the best reflective gear
articles.summary: Running before sunrise or after sunset requires extra safety precautions. Here’s the best reflective running gear and LED lights to protect yourself, plus expert tips.
articles.body: Running before the sun rises or after it sets may be the only time you can get a couple miles in — as a long distance runner myself, believe me, I’ve been there. Especially during the fall and winter when daylight hours are short, that means it’s very dark outside, increasing your risk of not being seen by drivers, cyclists and pedestrians. One of the best ways to stay safe when you head outside is to wear reflective running gear. It increases your visibility from up close and far away, and when you add other accessories like LED lights, it helps you see the path ahead better, too. Below, I talked to three experts about all the different types of reflective running gear and how to pick the best options for you. They also shared other safety tips for running in low light and total darkness, and broke down the important differences between reflective and fluorescent running gear. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. What is reflective running gear? Reflective running gear is technically made with retroreflective materials that bounce light directly back to its source, making the materials appear bright and more visible, says Dr. Milica McDowell, a doctor of physical therapy and the associate vice president at U.S. Physical Therapy. For example, a running vest made with retroreflective materials bounces a car’s headlights directly back to the driver, making the runner look bright so they’re more visible, says Anwen Davies, a certified personal trainer and fitness expert at Net World Sports. Retroreflective and reflective materials are technically two different things that vary in how light bounces off them. But “reflective” is how people commonly refer to running gear that makes you more visible in low light and total darkless, so that’s how I’m phrasing it here. The best reflective running gear, according to experts Reflective running gear makes you more visible to drivers, cyclists and pedestrians, but one piece of clothing or accessory is often not enough for people to notice you in low light and total darkness. Experts recommend wearing lights too, so I curated a list of both below. You’ll notice that many of the products on this list are neon-colored — that means they’re also fluorescent, which makes you more visible in daylight (learn the difference between reflective and fluorescent here). Best reflective running vest McDowell recommends wearing a reflective garment that covers your torso and arms if possible. “I prefer a reflective jacket or vest in order to create as much visibility in one of the largest parts of your body as possible, and it’s at eye-level for most pedestrians, cyclists and drivers,” she says. You can put this lightweight mesh vest on top of whatever you’re wearing to be more visible from all angles up to 800 feet away, according to the brand. There’s retroreflective materials on the front and back, and it comes with two adjustable reflective bands you can put on your arms, legs, wrists or ankles. The vest, which is available in small to extra extra large sizes, has an adjustable waistband and a large front zippered pocket to store essentials. Best LED running vest “I value pieces that are simple, lightweight and are visible from all directions such as this light-up vest from Amphipod,” says Jenny Simpson, the chief running officer for Fleet Feet. (Editor’s note: The inclusion of products sold by Fleet Feet in this article was made independently of Simpson.) “I wore it all throughout 2025 when my husband and I did our RUNUSA tour, living out of a van and running in all 50 states.” The vest is made from flexible adjustable, light-up cables and it weighs less than 3 ounces, so it won’t weigh you down. You can choose from eight light modes using a button on the back of the vest, including multiple colors, flashing lights and rainbow patterns. The vest’s battery lasts for up to 12 hours when it’s solid and 23 hours when it’s flashing (it comes with a USB-C charging cable). There’s also extra reflexive details on the sides that you can move around. Best reflective running belt I always wear a belt to store my essentials while running, so I might as well use one that’s reflective to increase my visibility. FlipBelt’s Zipper Running Belt comes in two reflective styles: neon yellow and black. There’s retroreflective material around the entire exterior, helping people see you from the front, sides and back. The belt, which you step into like pants, has a zippered pocket that I put my phone in, and you can access the other storage sleeves from two other access points — that’s how I stuff my gels, electrolyte tablets, hair ties and headphones inside, as well as store my keys with the built-in leash. Even when I run over 15 miles, this belt doesn’t bounce around or move once. Its fabric can get pretty damp with sweat, so I throw it in the washing machine at least once a week. It comes in XXS to XXL sizes. Best safety lights for running If you don’t want to invest in new clothing or accessories like vests, hats and belts, you should at least clip a LED light to yourself when running in low light or total darkness, experts say. These battery-powered, water-resistant LED safety lights come in a pack of two, so you always have a backup if one dies, especially in cold weather when batteries drain faster, says Davies. They weigh less than an ounce, come in multiple colors and are visible from over 1,000 feet away, according to the brand. The lights have clips that let you attach them to running belts, shirts, sports bra straps or hats, for example, and they come with three straps if you want to wear them around your arms, legs, wrists or ankles. You can choose from three light modes: solid, strobe and flash. Best headlamp for running Not only does a headlight make you more visible from the front, but it also illuminates your path. “You’re a lot more vulnerable if you can’t see the terrain ahead,” says Simpson. “Tripping and falling on a dark run invites even greater risk, so your ability to see the ground and what’s up ahead is very important to your safety.” Amphipod, a brand that Simpson and McDowell recommend, makes this headlight that clips onto any hat’s or visor’s brim. The light sits close to the base of the brim to keep your head comfortable and avoid getting in your way. It weighs less than 2 ounces and doesn’t bounce while you’re moving. There’s three brightness modes, and the light’s battery life lasts up to 6.5 hours, depending on which one you choose. When you plug it in, the light powers up in about two hours with the included USB-C cable. Best LED beanie This beanie keeps your head warm in cold weather, and the built-in LED light makes the path ahead of you more visible while helping drivers, cyclists and pedestrians see you from the front up to 30 feet away. The light pops off the hat and has a USB connector on it, letting you recharge it in a USB wall or car plug, a computer or a portable power bank. You can choose from three light modes by pressing the button on the front, and get up to four hours of continuous use on a full battery. The hat comes in over two dozen colors and patterns. Best reflective running shirt Rabbit has an impressive collection of reflective clothing for men and women, including this long-sleeve, lightweight thermal shirt. There’s a large pattern across the front and back of the shirt that’s made from retroreflective material, ensuring that people can see you from any angle. The shirt keeps you warm, is stretchy to move with your body and dries quickly as you sweat. It comes in women’s extra small to extra large sizes, and men’s small to extra large sizes. You can pair it with Rabbit’s matching reflective leggings, a jacket and gloves. How I picked the best reflective running gear To curate my list of the best reflective running gear, I focused on finding clothing and accessories that make runners the most visible to drivers, cyclists and pedestrians in low light and total darkness. I recommended gear made with large patches of retroreflective materials that cover key parts of the body, and gear that lights up, per experts’ recommendations. I chose products experts use themselves, as well as a few highly rated options that meet their guidance. How to shop for reflective running gear While shopping for reflective running gear, experts recommend considering the following factors. How to stay safe while running in low light or total darkness Wearing reflective running gear and lights aren’t the only safety precautions you should take while running in low light or total darkness. Here are other tips experts recommend. Don’t multitask: Running in low light or total darkness is not the time to wear noise-cancelling headphones, listen to music or talk on the phone, says McDowell. Be alert and fully aware of your surroundings at all times: You’re just as responsible for avoiding drivers, cyclists and pedestrians as they are for avoiding you, so eliminate distractions.Bring a fully charged phone: You can get directions or call for help if needed, plus your phone can track your location and share it with those you give permission to. Simpson also recommends bringing some form of identification.Choose a familiar route, and practice it in the daylight: Save experimenting with a new route for the daylight. When it’s dark out, stick to running in an area you’re familiar with and feel comfortable in. You should do a route in the daylight a few times before trying it in the dark to take note of obstacles and uneven terrain. That said, even a route you’ve done 100 times can be confusing in the dark, and landmarks look different without the sun illuminating them. Try to run in busier areas with bright storefronts, street lights and people around if you’re logging miles in low light or total darkness, says Davies.Run facing oncoming traffic: That’s the best way to make sure you see approaching drivers, cyclists and pedestrians, and they see you, says Davies. It’s also safer than ignoring or worrying about what’s behind you.Don’t assume drivers, cyclists or pedestrians see you: Just because you see a driver, cyclist or pedestrian doesn’t mean that they see you. If you’re approaching them, slow down, try to make eye contact and be prepared to get out of the way. That becomes even more important if you’re at an intersection or need to cross a road, which are highly vulnerable spots — drivers, cyclists and pedestrians are more likely to expect something coming from ahead or behind.Tell someone where you’re going, when you leave and when you expect to be back: That way someone notices if you’re late or don’t return at all, and can send help.Run with a buddy: Two pairs of eyes and ears are better than one when it comes to being aware of your surroundings. Also, if you’re both wearing reflective gear and lights, drivers, cyclists and pedestrians are more likely to see you, says Davies. What’s the difference between reflective and fluorescent running gear? There’s a big difference between reflective and fluorescent running gear. Reflective running gear is made with materials that bounce artificial light directly back to its source, making the gear appear bright. It makes you more visible in darkness.Fluorescent running gear comes in specific colors like neon orange, yellow, green and pink, which absorb UV light or daylight and re-emit it as super bright extra-visible light. It makes you more visible in daylight. Some running gear is reflective and fluorescent, which covers all your bases any time of day or night. Experts say it’s worth investing in these hybrid pieces to give yourself flexibility. Meet our experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Jenny Simpson is the chief running officer for Fleet Feet. (Editor’s note: The inclusion of products sold by Fleet Feet in this article was made independently of Simpson.)Dr. Milica McDowell is a doctor of physical therapy and the associate vice president at U.S. Physical Therapy.Anwen Davies is a certified personal trainer and fitness expert at Net World Sports. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered health and wellness for over six years. I extensively write about fitness and running, including topics like marathon essentials, women’s running shoes, running shoes with arch support, workout apps and dumbbell workouts. To write this article, I interviewed three experts about reflective running gear, how it works, why it’s important and how to find the best options. I’m also a long-distance runner, so I shared my own experiences about running in low light and total darkness and provided solutions that have worked for me. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Ex-Top Gear host Richard Hammond's new Abergavenny life wild swimming and food festivals
articles.summary: The former Top Gear star bought a 19th Century Georgian mansion near Abergavenny in November 2025.
articles.body:
Former Top Gear star Richard Hammond says he has swapped vintage cars for food festivals and running as he settles into life in a Welsh market town.

The 56-year-old bought a £2m Georgian mansion in Llanwenarth, near Abergavenny in Monmouthshire, in November 2025 following his divorce from wife Mindy after 23 years.

The presenter previously told BBC Wales he had "never been happier" since moving into the 19th Century home, and each week he has discovered a new reason to be "delighted that I live there".

With Bannau Brycheiniog - Brecon Beacons - in his back garden, Hammond told the High Performance Podcast he had taken up open water swimming as he becomes "braver" than he has ever been.

Hammond said it only took him a couple of visits to the property for him to realise that he "loved it".

"The Brecon Beacons National Park is the other side of my right-hand fence," he told the Telegraph.

"I can walk up the Sugar Loaf Mountain in an hour and 20 minutes or I could be getting measured for a new suit or buying a coffee in 20 minutes."

His home is currently being renovated to include car garages, a padel court and guest accommodation.

He recently made headlines for saying he would "find a way" to share his space with rare bats that have paused his renovation plans.

He said: "I just have to work with the bats. I like bats. You don't move to where I've moved and try to stamp all the nature out."

At the beginning of 2025, Hammond announced that he and his wife Mindy, who share two children, were separating, just three months after his father died of cancer.

It also came around the time of the final Grand Tour episode which brought his 22-year broadcasting career with Jeremy Clarkson and James May to an end.

Since then, he has been rebuilding his life in Wales, and said his energy levels had "been replenished".

"I'm now far braver and do things I would never have done," he said.

He has even joined an Abergavenny running club, bringing his 5k time down to under 25 minutes, and taken up open water swimming in the Lake District as he keeps pace with new girlfriend Keira "Kiki" Glen.

"Basically, she did a triathlon and I went to support her," he told the Telegraph.

"They were all having such a great time and buzzing afterwards, so I signed up for next year and got swept along."

While you would expect that classic cars and motor racing still feature heavily in his life, Hammond is aware that his priorities have shifted.

Rather than attending the Goodwood Revival festival this year, he was sampling cheeses and whiskies at the Abergavenny Food Festival.

Hammond is probably best-known for his time on Top Gear, which was revived in 2002, and went on to become one of the BBC's flagship shows at the time.

But he was unsure whether the formula would work today because it was a "completely different time".

In August, it was announced the show, which has been off air since Andrew "Freddie" Flintoff was seriously injured in a crash while filming four years ago, is coming back .

"The BBC will bring it back because it's an old brand, it predates us by decades," Hammond said.

"The car is the second biggest outlay people have."

Hammond's daughter Izzy has inherited her father's love of cars and the pair now co-present on the social media channel DriveTribe.

Hammond said he was "sure" she would be interested in a role on Top Gear some day.

"It'd be good to see some females on those shows," he said.

"Half the drivers are. TV has a role to play in representation. It's important, nobody's going to step into an arena unless they see somebody that represents them."

articles.title: Texas Republican group seeks to block certification of state’s election
articles.summary: Republicans in a Texas county have filed a lawsuit asking for ballots in the state’s midterm races to be hand-counted.
articles.body:
Days before the United States’ pivotal midterm elections, a Texas group affiliated with the Republican Party has asked a federal judge to stop certification of the state’s upcoming election results.

In a lawsuit filed on Tuesday, the Potter County Republican Party and its chairman, Daniel Rogers, claim potential election interference by artificial intelligence (AI) or “malicious actors” that could compromise the results of next Tuesday’s elections in Texas.

The plaintiffs, who are asking for a hand count of every ballot from every precinct in the state before election certification happens, allege voting machines have components inside made by China that would allow them to be manipulated.

“If a component is tampered with during manufacturing, it could serve as a point of entry for unlawful and malfeasance hackers, allowing for the possibility of synchronized attacks across multiple election machines and jurisdictions,” the lawsuit read.

The legal challenge comes as several polls show Democrat James Talarico narrowly leading his Republican challenger, Ken Paxton, in Texas’ all-important US Senate race that could ultimately decide which party controls the chamber after November 3.

The Talarico and Paxton campaigns and the Potter County Republican Party did not immediately return requests from Al Jazeera for comment.

The legal complaint does not specify if any voting machines in Potter County, or elsewhere in Texas, have been compromised. The plaintiffs acknowledged in their filing that no previous election in the county was “altered” by a third party, arguing that the possibility of vote manipulation by AI makes the state’s election safeguards easily compromised.

“The real likelihood of a clever and undetected hack by recently developed AI programs, which conceal their activity to avoid detection, reinforces the need for a full verification based on hand-counting of all paper records or ballots in all Texas precincts, prior to certification of the federal results,” they wrote.

State law in Texas already requires hand-count audits in elections where electronic tabulators are used. But the plaintiffs argue that does not go far enough.

“The paper record or ballot provides an independent verification mechanism only if election officials actually compare a complete hand count of all of the paper records or ballots,” the filing said.

The lawsuit also claims US “adversaries”, such as China, Iran and Russia, are capable of accessing election systems.

US President Donald Trump in July declassified documents that, he claimed, showed Chinese interference in the US 2020 presidential election, reviving his attacks on US elections despite no evidence that Beijing impacted the vote he lost that year.

Last week, the US Department of Justice also sought to block certification of an election, claiming, in Alaska, that an independent candidate with the same name as the state’s Republican Senator up for re-election is running in order to mislead voters.

Alicia Pierce, a spokeswoman for Texas’s Secretary of State, whose office administers elections in the state, said it “does not plan to comment on the lawsuit at this time”.

articles.title: Canada 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski found guilty of fraud
articles.summary: Prosecutors had accused Pleterski of stealing tens of millions of dollars of investor funds to buy himself a range of luxuries.
articles.body:
A Toronto jury has found self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski guilty of fraud, after hearing evidence he stole millions of dollars of investor money and spent it on private jets and other luxuries.

The jury quickly reached its verdict on Thursday, convicting the 27-year-old with one count of fraud over C$5,000 ($3,600; £2,900), after just hours of deliberation.

Throughout trial, Crown prosecutors called over a dozen witnesses, including investors whom Pleterski had cheated, and accountants and financial experts who testified on his scheme.

Pleterski pleaded not guilty and represented himself at his trial, cross-examining only one witness. He presented no evidence and did not testify.

The Canadian man was charged in May 2024 with one count each of fraud and money laundering following a 16-month joint investigation between Durham Regional Police and the Ontario Securities Commission.

The laundering charge was later dropped.

At the time, Durham Regional Police Chief Peter Moreira said it was potentially the biggest-ever fraud case in the region.

During Pleterski's trial in Ontario's Superior Court, Crown prosecutors presented ample evidence of his lavish spending using investor funds, according to local media.

He is believed to have taken more than C$36m from investors, and spent about half.

They said he used the money sent to his company AP Private Equity Limited to buy multiple trips on private jets and spend about C$5.6m on luxury vehicles.

Prosecutors also said he used the money to spend C$45,000 a month on a lakefront mansion in Burlington, Ontario, while racking up C$4.9m in credit card bills.

Bankruptcy proceedings had shown Pleterski also bought a McLaren and BMW for his parents - who had given him C$50,000 as a crypto investment - along with a Louis Vuitton bag, Burberry coat and a 2017 Bentley Bentayga.

Crown prosecutor Akshay Aurora said during closing arguments on Wednesday that "Pleterski was no 'Crypto King'".

"He was a thief. A thief who stole investor money and used it as he pleased," Aurora told the jury, according to CBC News.

Things came crashing down for Pleterski ahead of his May 2024 arrest.

In December 2022, he was kidnapped in the middle of the night in downtown Toronto, with his captors demanding a large sum for his release.

"I'm sorry, I really am, I didn't want to or mean to ruin anyone's life," a bruised and bloodied Pleterski said in a video obtained by CBC News.

He was released three days later, after being tortured, including with waterboarding, cigarette burns and beatings with golf clubs.

He returns to court on 13 November for a sentencing hearing.

articles.title: Pentagon fires general it says leaked classified information to media
articles.summary: Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was subject of investigation into leaking information about Iran and Ukraine.
articles.body:
United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the director of the Strategy, Plans and Policy Directorate at the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, for what the Pentagon says is severe misconduct. The move comes amid reports that the US had warned its allies of a possible renewal of strikes against Iran.

A Department of Defense official told Al Jazeera on Thursday that Sylvia had been “meeting with journalists outside the Pentagon in order to leak classified information”.

“Sylvia is the subject of an investigation for leaking classified information about the Iran war, the war between Russia and Ukraine, and more,” the official added.

The investigation into Sylvia remains ongoing and has been referred to the Department of Justice for further action, according to the Pentagon.

The official said Sylvia was the Defense Department’s chief military planner but “was not a central planner for the Iran war”. “That is the responsibility of CENTCOM [Central Command] and its commander, Admiral [Brad] Cooper,” the official said.

Sylvia’s firing comes as Trump has repeatedly floated starting new military operations against Iran.

He is the second person to be ousted from the post, known in military circles as the J5, under Hegseth. His predecessor was forced to retire in October last year.

“Sylvia failed three polygraphs which questioned him about leaking classified information,” the Pentagon official said while accusing Sylvia of putting national security at risk.

“Urgent action was needed and could not wait another second,” he concluded.

There is no immediate replacement for Sylvia, according to an official who spoke on the condition of anonymity to The Associated Press news agency.

Before arriving at the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Sylvia served as commander of the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, until May 2025, according to his official biography, which has now been taken offline. He also previously served as the vice director for the office he recently led.

His military awards include six Bronze Star Medals, including one for valour, and a Purple Heart, indicating he was wounded in combat.

Sean Parnel, assistant to the defense secretary for public affairs, said earlier on Thursday in a post on X that “the Department of War has zero tolerance for the intentional, unauthorized disclosure of classified information.” He did not refer specifically to Sylvia.

Sylvia is the latest senior Pentagon official whom Hegseth has accused of leaking to the media. He fired three aides from his inner circle last year as part of a broader leak investigation that included polygraph tests.

President Donald Trump has promised to “finish the job” in Iran after launching the war with Israel eight months ago and said he would do so after the midterm elections on Tuesday.

articles.title: Drilling for water on his Texas farm, Fritz Fuchs hit oil at 300 feet; a deeper test followed, and leases paid $84,000 in cash plus a 1/6 royalty on 482 acres
articles.summary: Discover how Fritz Fuchs' search for water on his Texas farm led to an unexpected oil boom that transformed a small town and created economic opportunities for struggling farmers in 1915.
articles.body: Williamson County farmers were considering water rather than oil in 1914. The area had been dried by a drought; the local economy relied heavily on cotton and livestock, with about 150 people living in the little town of Thrall, which was located on the railway some six miles east of Taylor. An excellent well becomes a farm's most important asset when the rain stops. Based on this, farmer Fritz Fuchs chose to drill for water in the southwest corner of his 100-acre farm. In a 1921 article in the AAPG Bulletin, he stated he found little or no water but abundant oil in the well at a depth of 300 feet. That little surprise changed the fortunes of the town and, for a few frenetic years, much of the county around it.From water well to discovery wellA water well that produces oil might look like a disappointment today but an opportunity tomorrow. By early February 1915, preparations had been made to drill deeper, and on 22 February, the discovery well was in. Williamson County's history describes the discovery well as possibly the first drilled in the Serpentine formation. It was on the Fuchs property about a mile south of town. Read Williamson County's history of Thrall. Nobody had set out to find oil on that farm. The drill was meant to solve a farming problem, and the same hole that disappointed its owner on the water question ended up answering a much bigger one.Cash rented by farmersOnce oil was discovered, farmers struggling through the 1914 drought could lease land for cash. A contemporary account reported that Fritz Fuchs received $84,400 for a lease covering 482 acres, along with a one-sixth royalty on oil and gas produced. Read the archived contemporary account of the lease. This was a favourable arrangement because a one-sixth royalty gave the landowner a larger share than the one-eighth royalty common in many oil leases. The original discovery well, however, is described in another account as being on a 100-acre farm. The available records do not fully explain the relationship between that farm and the later lease covering 482 acres, so the two figures should not be treated as the same parcel.The 1915 discovery attracted oil operators and other visitors to the field. Williamson County's history names Alf Landon, who later became the Republican presidential nominee in 1936, among those who visited, alongside Harry J. Sinclair, who founded the Sinclair Petroleum Corporation, and J. L. Lattimer, who later became president of Magnolia Petroleum. The historical account does not give a precise date for each visit, so Landon's later political role should not be mistaken for a position he held during the 1915 discovery.University geologists later studied the field. Halbert P. Bybee worked for the University of Texas Bureau of Economic Geology during the summers of 1915 and 1916. In 1916, J. A. Udden and H. P. Bybee published The Thrall Oil Field, a Bureau bulletin documenting the geology of the field and the oil-bearing formations associated with the discovery.A boom that went bustThe boom dramatically changed Thrall. The town had about 150 residents in 1914 and grew to as many as 3,000 during the oil rush before its population fell to 272 by 1920. About 200 wells were drilled in the area, and the first hundred were described as gushers. Williamson County's history records that the field proved shallow and that most wells had failed by 1940, although a few were still producing modest amounts in 1973.Lease bonuses provided landowners with cash up front, while later income depended on how long the wells continued producing. A separate surge of activity took place near Thrall in 1930, when a well on the J. C. Abbott property brought renewed drilling interest. Williamson County's history says crowds in Taylor doubled and more than 1,500 leases were signed in less than three days during that later surge. Those lease signings should not be attributed to the initial 1915 discovery.In 1914, Fritz Fuchs set out to find water on his farm and instead encountered oil, helping trigger one of Texas's early oil booms. The discovery brought lease income to farmers struggling with drought and attracted oil operators and geologists to Williamson County. articles.title: IAS Shikhar Agrawal placed under APO amid villa purchase allegations
articles.summary: Rajasthan IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal put under APO after media allegations that his family bought 40 villas/cottages; govt cites administrative reasons, no probe confirmed.
articles.body: Jaipur: Rajasthan govt Wednesday placed senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal under awaiting posting order (APO) amid allegations that he, his IPS officer wife Prashakha Mathur, their two sons and parents-in-law purchased 40 villas and cottages from the same company over a period of two-and-a-half years. The allegations were reported by a local newspaper.According to an order issued by the personnel department late Wednesday night, Agrawal, a 1993-batch IAS officer, has been placed under APO until further orders for administrative reasons.Agrawal was serving as additional chief secretary (ACS) of industries, MSME, planning and other departments. He also held the posts of chairperson of Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation (RIICO) and managing director of RAJSICO.Agrawal could not be contacted despite repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the allegations and his removal from the post. Chief Secretary V Srinivas and ACS to the chief minister Akhil Arora also did not respond to calls and messages. Officials in Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said there was no official confirmation yet on whether an inquiry or an internal probe would be initiated into the allegations against Agrawal.One of the senior-most IAS officers in the state, Agrawal, had earlier served in CMO. He was removed from CMO following reports of differences with former chief secretary Sudhansh Pant. The tussle between the two over transfer of officials and allegations of files being bypassed had become a major talking point in the corridors of power. Many believe this to be one of the reasons for Pant opting for central deputation.Despite being seventh in the seniority pecking order among IAS officers in the state, Agrawal was among the contenders for the chief secretary’s post after Srinivas’s scheduled retirement in Feb 2027. articles.title: Cyclone Arnab brings rain, chill to Raj
articles.summary: Cyclone Arnab weakens into deep depression, bringing rain and thunderstorms to Rajasthan; Jaipur sees showers as temperatures may drop 3-5°C.
articles.body: Times News NetworkJaipur: Several parts of Rajasthan witnessed mild to moderate rainfall Thursday as the weather system associated with cyclonic storm Arnab weakened into a deep depression.India Meteorological Department (IMD) Jaipur has forecast rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms at several places in Jaipur, Bharatpur, Ajmer, Kota and Udaipur divisions over the next couple of days.The Met office has also indicated that maximum and minimum temperatures across the state may fall by 3-5°C, bringing a further chill to several areas.The rainfall activity has been attributed to the deep depression associated with Cyclone Arnab which has affected Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan.Jaipur woke up to a relatively cool morning with the minimum temperature settling at 22°C. Cloudy conditions prevailed during the afternoon, when the maximum temperature was recorded at 27.4°C, nearly 5°C below normal. Several parts of the city, including Tonk Road, Bapu Nagar, Tilak Nagar, Malviya Nagar and Jagatpura, witnessed showers in the evening.Moderate to heavy rainfall was also reported from several areas of Sikar, Alwar, Bharatpur, Ajmer and Kotputli-Behror districts.Fatehpur and Nagaur emerged among the coldest places in the state, with a minimum temperature of 11.3°C recorded. Among other locations, Pilani recorded a minimum of 15°C, followed by Bhilwara at 16.8°C, Sriganganagar at 17.3°C and Banasthali at 17.6°C. Ajmer recorded a minimum temperature of 18°C, while Chittorgarh and Bikaner registered 18.2°C each.In contrast, western Rajasthan continued to experience relatively warmer daytime conditions. Barmer recorded a maximum temperature of 35.8°C, followed by Jodhpur at 34.3°C and Jaisalmer at 34.2°C.
